title: Call for nationwide peaceful demonstrations over disputed election results; execution unverified
location: Uganda; no specific assembly venue reported
scope: Nationwide call; any executed gathering and its scope are unknown
organizer: Bobi Wine (Robert Kyagulanyi), as reported by VOA Swahili
threshold_50_evidence: No gathering or attendance is reported; the 50-person threshold cannot be assessed.

title.summary: The source reports a call for peaceful demonstrations against alleged election-result fraud; it does not report an assembly.

organizer.summary: The report attributes the call to Bobi Wine.

demands.summary: The call concerns alleged election-result fraud and a constitutional right to demonstrate, fitting political_behavior_process.

start_date.summary: No physical gathering date is reported; the article's January 22 publication/call date is not adopted as event onset.

participants_original.summary: No attendees or turnout are reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No physical gathering is reported, so attendance and threshold remain unknown.

state_response.summary: No gathering-specific state action is reported; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

notes: This is a source-only lead for an announced call, not evidence of an executed public assembly. Do not infer that the demonstration occurred, when or where it began, turnout, state response, violence, or an end. The report says the call was made on January 22, 2021; that date belongs to the announcement, not a physical protest. Follow up on whether and where any gathering actually took place. Treat this VOA Swahili report as one newsroom origin, not independent corroboration of a related VOA report.
open_questions: Was any public assembly held in response to the call?
If held, when and where did it start, how many attended, and what own-state demand was made?

title: Reported January 16 election-result protests in Luwero and Masaka; event unit unresolved
location: Luwero District and Masaka, Uganda; exact venues not reported
scope: One Reuters report describes protests in two areas on the same day; whether these were separate events or one coordinated episode is unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: The report identifies protests in two areas but gives no attendance count or qualitative crowd size and says no other details were immediately available. The at-least-50 threshold cannot be assessed at either site.

title.summary: The opened Reuters byline report describes protests following announcement of Uganda's presidential election results in Luwero and Masaka.

start_date.summary: The article was published January 18 and dates the protests to Saturday after Thursday's election and the Saturday results announcement; the relative date maps to January 16.

end_date.summary: No dissolution, departure, or physical end is reported; the story says no other details were immediately available.

location.summary: The article names Luwero district north of Kampala and Masaka to the southwest, with no particular venues or site-level details.

scope.summary: The single report says protests occurred in two areas on January 16; it does not establish coordination or whether to code one or two local event units.

organizer.summary: No protest organizer is identified. The NUP official is quoted about a planned court challenge, not as an organizer of the protests.

demands.summary: The story characterizes the protests as being over the announced election result; it gives no detailed protester statement or site-specific demand.

participants_original.summary: No attendance estimate or participant count is reported.

participants_min.summary: No numerical or qualitative evidence supports a minimum attendance.

participants_max.summary: No numerical or qualitative evidence supports a maximum attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The source reports protests but gives no crowd size or attendance description; the threshold cannot be verified.

protester_violence.summary: No participant conduct is described; this dimension remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The Reuters report attributes two deaths to security forces and reports 23 arrests in total, citing NTV Uganda and local police. It does not assign either outcome to a district or identify the arrested people as protesters individually; the response is one source-reported aggregate across the two-area account.

notes: One contemporary Reuters report, republished by The Fiji Times on January 18, describes protests in Luwero and Masaka on January 16 after the election result announcement. It attributes two deaths and 23 arrests to NTV Uganda citing local police, but reports no other protest details, crowd size or venues. A matching DefenceWeb article is the same Reuters story; the two Reddit results are search-only copies/leads and are not independent corroboration. Event occurrence is reported, but attendance threshold, site-specific state action and one-versus-two event unit remain unresolved.
open_questions: Do Luwero and Masaka represent separate assemblies or one coordinated episode, and what were the exact venues?
Did either location reach 50 participants, and is any independently authored contemporary account available?
Can the reported deaths and 23 arrests be assigned to particular events or identified participants?
